record.paper_title: Seven open problems in applied combinatorics
record.original_question: Let G=(V,E,ω) be a weighted simple graph, let W=V be the witness set, and let L⊂V be an ε-net. The Dowker complex Dow_α(W,L) is the simplicial complex on the landmark set L whose simplices are the subsets σ⊂L for which there exists a witness w∈W satisfying d_G(w,l)≤α for every l∈σ. Determine how to choose ε and how to select the ε-net L so that, for sufficiently large α, the one-dimensional persistence diagram PD_1(Dow_α(W,L)) has cardinality equal to the genus of G. Assuming such an ε-net is given, find a bound for the bottleneck distance d_B(PD_1(VR_α(G)), PD_1(Dow_α(W,L))) in terms of the cycle lengths of G and ε.

evidence.quote: Definition 1.4 (Dowker Complex). Let G = (V, E, ω) be a weighted simple graph with induced geodesic distance dG, and let L, W ⊂ V. For α ∈ R≥0, let Dowα(W, L) be the abstract simplicial complex with set of vertices L and a simplex σ ∈ Dowα(W, L) if and only if there exists w ∈ W such that dG(w, l) ≤ α for all l ∈ σ.

Open Problem 1.3. Let G = (V, E, ω) be weighted simple graph. Take the set of witnesses W = V. (i) Determine  > 0 and the way to select an -net L ⊂ V such that PD1(Dowα(W, L)) has cardinality equal to the genus of G, for a sufficiently large value α. (ii) Assuming that an -net for G satisfying (i) is given. Find a bound for dB(PD1(VRα(G)), PD1(Dowα(W, L))), in terms of the lengths of cycles in G and , where dB is the bottleneck distance in persistence diagrams.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G = (V, E, \omega)$ be a weighted simple graph with positive edge weights $\omega: E \to \mathbb{R}_{>0}$, and let $d_G : V \times V \to \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ denote the induced shortest-path (geodesic) distance on $V$. For $\varepsilon > 0$, an $\varepsilon$-net is a subset $L \subset V$ such that (i) for every $v \in V$ there exists $\ell \in L$ with $d_G(v,\ell) \le \varepsilon$, and (ii) $d_G(\ell, \ell') > \varepsilon$ for all distinct $\ell, \ell' \in L$.

For $\alpha \ge 0$, define the Vietoris–Rips complex $\operatorname{VR}_\alpha(G)$ as the abstract simplicial complex on vertex set $V$ whose simplices are the finite subsets $\sigma \subset V$ with $d_G(v,v') \le \alpha$ for all $v,v' \in \sigma$. Let $W = V$ (the "witness" set). Define the Dowker complex
$$\operatorname{Dow}_\alpha(W, L) = \{ \sigma \subset L : \exists\, w \in W \text{ with } d_G(w,\ell) \le \alpha \text{ for every } \ell \in \sigma \}.$$

As $\alpha$ varies, both $\{\operatorname{VR}_\alpha(G)\}_\alpha$ and $\{\operatorname{Dow}_\alpha(W,L)\}_\alpha$ form filtrations of simplicial complexes; let $\operatorname{PD}_1(\cdot)$ denote the resulting one-dimensional persistence diagram. Let $d_B$ denote the bottleneck distance between persistence diagrams, and let $g(G)$ denote the (orientable) genus of the graph $G$.

(i) Determine a rule prescribing a value $\varepsilon > 0$ and a procedure for selecting an $\varepsilon$-net $L \subset V$ such that, for all sufficiently large $\alpha$,
$$\#\,\operatorname{PD}_1(\operatorname{Dow}_\alpha(W, L)) \;=\; g(G).$$

(ii) Under the assumption that $L$ is an $\varepsilon$-net satisfying (i), establish an explicit upper bound for
$$d_B\bigl(\operatorname{PD}_1(\operatorname{VR}_\alpha(G)),\, \operatorname{PD}_1(\operatorname{Dow}_\alpha(W, L))\bigr)$$
expressed in terms of $\varepsilon$ and the lengths of cycles of $G$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in a 2023 survey on open problems in applied combinatorics. Web searches reveal related stability results for Dowker and Vietoris–Rips persistence diagrams and applications of Dowker complexes, but no source addresses this specific question of choosing an ε-net so that the cardinality of PD_1 of the Dowker complex equals the genus of the graph, nor a bottleneck-distance bound in terms of cycle lengths and ε. No subsequent work resolving the problem was located.

status_evidence.title: A functorial Dowker theorem and persistent homology of asymmetric networks
status_evidence.snippet: Provides functorial Dowker theorems and stability results for Dowker persistence diagrams, but does not address the genus-cardinality identification or the specific bottleneck bound posed.
status_evidence.claim: Related stability and functoriality results exist for Dowker persistence, but the specific problem remains unaddressed.

status_evidence.title: An approach based on Dowker filtrations
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Dowker filtrations and comparisons with Vietoris–Rips, without resolving the ε-net selection / genus problem.
status_evidence.claim: No resolution of the genus-via-Dowker problem was found in the Dowker filtration literature.
